status: Recovery-resolution screening; no measured damping or repetition limit for our designs

source.paper: Physics-Based Nozzle Design Rules for High-Frequency Liquid Metal Jetting
source.relevant_scope: Pinned-meniscus aluminum nozzle models; oscillatory wall layers and geometry-dependent recovery. Not our solder/free-level/slit/contact-line configuration.

scaling: delta~sqrt(nu/omega); frequencies here are exploratory rad/s values, not measured frequencies of our nozzle.

rest_to_rest_example.scope: An illustrative fully-settled-before-next-pulse criterion, not a user requirement or necessary bound. Phase-controlled periodic operation can use residual motion.

implications: The50umgrid can resolve a0.5mmdrop across10cells while still under-resolving a roughly7..23um viscous wall layer. Single-drop size checks therefore do not qualify recovery/damping/rate.
Five milliseconds of conditioning need not mean equilibrium. Compare common initial histories and record the phase/meniscus state at drive onset.

Maintain the distinction between a clean single pulse and stable periodic jetting. Measure meniscus recovery or simulate an adequately validated periodic state before claiming hundreds of drops per second.
Geometry changes that increase wetted area per active fluid volume may aid damping, at a cost in pressure loss and manufacture. No extra internal structures are adopted without a practical benefit.
